question: According to my personal development notes, what are the three components of career success and how much does each matter?

retrieved.text:
Personal development
Minimum likeability threshold to even be considered for a project. Hence the important of building relationships
Performance, image, and exposure (who knows you) are the three components to success
10% performance, image (30%) and exposure (60%) are more critical
Networks
Dunbar’s number is 150 (average network size). Can be stratified by emotional intensity
5: innermost circle
15: sympathy group
50: close friends
150: casual friends
450-600: acquaintances
King – 3 basic categories of networks
Expansionists who are well connected with extraordinarily large networks. Can’t leverage ties as well
Identify super-connecters and develop relationships with them!!!
Reciprocity is important; try to offer things in relationships
Brokers generate value by brining together typically disconnected parties from different social worlds. Bring information benefits. Smaller number of deeper links

The need for achievement is the need to achieve personal goals and success. Octopus’ practices satisfy employees’ nAch by allocating 30% of working hours to self-selected projects and personal development. Presuming these self-selected tasks are performed successfully, employees will be able to achieve their personal goals. Second, the need for power refers to the need to influence the behaviour of others. Octopus employees can satisfy their nPow by leading their own projects because, in doing so, they will instruct their colleagues to perform tasks in pursuit of their self-selected goal. Third, the need for affiliation is the need for employees to have close interpersonal relationships. nAff is comparable to Maslow’s belongingness need; Octopus’ social gatherings should satisfy employees’ nAff as these environments are conducive to relationship-forming.

Moving up the hierarchy, esteem needs include the desire for self-respect and peer recognition. Octopus allows employees to spend 30% of working hours on personal development, or creating and leading their own projects. Employees can develop their self-respect by improving their skills through personal development, and can also gain peer recognition where selected to lead their own projects. To further satisfy esteem needs, Octopus’ managers should recognise the success of employee-led projects. These same policies will also satisfy employees’ need for self-actualisation. The freedom to pursue personal development, perhaps guided by a mentor, will enable employees to achieve their full potential. The freedom to design their own projects empowers employees to implement their own creative ideas, another component of self-actualisation.

Octopus’ practices satisfy Maslow’s higher -order needs; therefore, this theory would conclude its employees will be highly motivated. McClelland's Three Needs Theory McClelland posits individuals are universally motivated by the need for achievement (nAch), power (nPow) and affiliation (nAff) (Robbins and Judge, 2019).
